chief_complaint: heavy prolonged periods and pelvic pressure
hpi_details: A 23-year-old female presents to the clinic with heavy prolonged periods and pelvic pressure. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: thinks it might be related to fibroids
concerns: worried about potential complications and long term recovery
expectations: wants complete diagnostic evaluation and treatment plan

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Uterine leiomyomas (fibroids) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Uterine Leiomyomas: Check CBC, transvaginal ultrasound, discuss hormonal vs myomectomy, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Key HPI features: A 23-year-old female presents to the clinic with heavy prolonged periods and pelvic pressure. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Uterine Leiomyomas.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Uterine leiomyomas (fibroids).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Adenomyosis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Prolonged heavy bleeding.
management_principles: Plan for Uterine Leiomyomas: Check CBC, transvaginal ultrasound, discuss hormonal vs myomectomy
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with heavy prolonged periods, pelvic pressure, and fatigue; further history and examination are needed to identify the cause.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Uterine Leiomyomas.
reference_soap.assessment: Abnormal uterine bleeding with pelvic pressure; evaluate for leiomyomas and other structural, endocrine, and pregnancy-related causes.
reference_soap.plan: Assess hemodynamic stability, obtain a pregnancy test and CBC, and arrange pelvic ultrasound. Select medical or procedural management only after diagnosis, bleeding severity, fertility goals, and contraindications are established.
